team.name: dream-team
team.description: Stack-agnostic multi-agent development team for Claude Code. Invoke with /team <task>.

CAPABILITIES.md.note: Describes this machine, not this repository: which optional capabilities are installed and how the team may use them. Rewritten by every /team-setup run. Absent or empty means the team runs with none, which is a supported state.

hooks.purpose: Sticky team mode: while the marker file exists, every user prompt is routed back through the /team orchestrator, surviving model switches, pauses, compaction and restarts.
hooks.requires: a bash shell (Git Bash or WSL on Windows); without one the hook exits quietly and sticky mode is simply unavailable

pluginPolicy.consent: Every plugin in this list is optional and is installed only after the user agrees to that specific plugin. /team-setup reports what is missing and asks before installing anything. /team and the subagents never install, enable or disable a plugin.
pluginPolicy.degradation: The team must produce the same quality of work with none of these installed. A capability is an accelerator, never a prerequisite. An agent that cannot see a capability proceeds without it and never tells the user something was impossible because a plugin was absent.
pluginPolicy.brokering: Subagents run with the tool list in their own frontmatter, which does not include tools contributed by plugins. By default the orchestrator uses a capability itself and passes the result into the handoff. A team owner who wants an agent to call a capability directly must add that capability's tools to the agent's frontmatter; /team-setup reports which agents would need that and never edits them.
pluginPolicy.verification: Install identifiers below were confirmed against the official marketplace listing and the vendors' own installation instructions in September 2026. Re-check before relying on one; /team-setup reports what is actually installed rather than trusting this file.

plugins.name: context7
plugins.alternativeInstall: claude mcp add --scope user context7 -- npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp
plugins.useWhen: The task depends on a third-party library or framework and the exact current signature, option name, or version-specific behaviour is not visible in this repository. Look it up before designing or writing the call, not after it fails.
plugins.neverUseFor: Anything about this project's own code, conventions or commands — those come from .claude/knowledge/ and the repository itself. Fetched documentation never overrides an observed project convention; when they disagree, the repository wins and the disagreement is reported.

plugins.name: claude-mem
plugins.install: /plugin marketplace add thedotmack/claude-mem, then /plugin install claude-mem
plugins.detect: a tool or command whose name contains "mem", contributed by this plugin
plugins.useWhen: At preflight, to recall the user's standing preferences and what earlier sessions concluded about this project. Treat every recollection as a hint to verify, never as a fact.
plugins.neverUseFor: Storing the team's own learnings. LEARNINGS.md stays the single compounding record: it is reviewable, project-scoped and lives beside the code. Never let a recollection outrank the repository or the knowledge files.

plugins.name: claude-md-management
plugins.detect: a command for revising the project instruction file, contributed by this plugin
plugins.useWhen: At the docs-sync step of a run that changed a documented rule or created a new obligation: propose the instruction-file update through this capability and let the user approve the diff.
plugins.neverUseFor: Editing project instruction files silently or in the middle of a run, and regenerating PROJECT-RULES.md — that belongs to the knowledge generator, which reads the instruction file rather than writing it.

plugins.name: chrome-devtools-mcp
plugins.detect: a tool for navigating, inspecting or screenshotting a live browser page
plugins.useWhen: A run changed something a person sees and the result can be observed by loading the running application: the Tester needs a check against real rendering, the Reviewer needs to confirm the change actually appears, or a diagnosis needs the real console or network behaviour.
plugins.neverUseFor: Projects with no user interface; starting a server or opening a page without the user agreeing first; and never as a substitute for a test — a screenshot is evidence, not coverage.

plugins.name: playwright
plugins.marketplace: (not published as a marketplace plugin as of September 2026)
plugins.detect: a tool for driving a browser through structured page data
plugins.useWhen: Same as the other browser-control entry. Install at most one of the two: two browser drivers competing for the same page waste context and produce contradictory observations.
plugins.neverUseFor: Same exclusions as the other browser-control entry.

checks.runFrom: team root (this directory; in an installed project: .claude/team)
checks.note: "hook" is deliberately absent from this pattern: it is a Claude Code harness term the team must be able to name. React's hooks are caught by useState/useEffect instead.
checks.stackNeutralityLint: grep -n -i -E "\b(go|golang|python|java|c#|csharp|dotnet|typescript|javascript|node|react|angular|vue|redux|usestate|useeffect|selector|slice|controller|mediatr|cqrs|linq|dbcontext|prisma|sqlalchemy|xunit|nunit|jest|vitest|pytest|npm|pip|nuget|cargo|csproj|axios|fetch|swagger|openapi|gofmt|eslint|prettier|nullable|eager.?load|n\+1|re-?render|functional component|any types|router)\b" agents/*.md skills/*/SKILL.md README.md
